title: Three timing flakes share one trigger: full-workspace parallel load
description:
2026-11-26. Three different tests failed once each across today's gate
runs, each passing 3 of 3 in isolation afterwards. All three wait for an
event and time out, and all three only fail under
`cargo test --workspace --all-features`.

## The instances

1. mimid-gn1w: `stock_rust_client_chats_through_two_daemons`. "no
   StateChange on the reconnecting stream in 15s; no frames arrived at
   all". Isolated: 2.75s. Under load: timed out at 15s.
2. mimid-h5c2: `a_call_in_a_chat_of_more_than_two_is_refused`. A call
   that should have been refused for having three participants was
   created, so the serving path saw a stale participant list.
3. `calls_across_two_providers` (crates/mimid-agent/tests/calls.rs).
   "no line from the server in time". Isolated: 3.4s, three times.
   Under load: failed after 35.5s.

## Why one bead

The common factor is not the code under test -- an SSE stream, a VTC
policy check and an IRC line have little to do with each other -- it is
that each waits on another task making progress, and under the full run
there are around 114 test binaries competing for 18 threads. A fix that
works for one probably works for all three, and three separate
"increase the timeout" patches would hide all three.

Instance 2 is the one that is not obviously only a test problem: a stale
participant read would be a real defect in a policy check, which is why
mimid-h5c2 is filed separately at P1 and stays open on its own terms.

## What to do, in order

1. Measure rather than guess: run the suite with
   `--test-threads` reduced and see whether the flakes stop. If they do,
   the waits are too short for the load, not wrong.
2. Prefer waiting on a condition over a fixed deadline where the test
   harness allows it. The helper at
   crates/mimid-agent/tests/common/irc.rs:118 and the SSE helper are the
   two places to start, since they are shared by many tests.
3. Only then consider longer deadlines, and say in the message what the
   wait was for, as mimid-gn1w's improved message now does -- that
   message is what told us "no frames arrived at all" and ruled out a
   publish/subscribe race.

Do not mark any of the three resolved on the strength of passing in
isolation. That is how all three got here.
